activities.title: Core language and control flow in one script
activities.purpose: Establish the foundational syntax and control flow needed before any data processing can be written.
activities.instructions: Work through a beginner Python tutorial or course covering variables, numeric types, strings, string formatting, booleans, if/elif/else, while loops and for loops. After each concept, write a tiny script that uses it. Then write one script that reads a few lines of text input, branches on a condition and loops over the lines to print a formatted result. Run it and fix any errors until it behaves as expected.
activities.completionCriterion: A single script that uses variables, at least one conditional, one while or for loop and formatted output, runs without errors and produces the expected result on two different inputs.

activities.title: Collections and functions for record handling
activities.purpose: Build the data structures and function skills required to represent and transform records.
activities.instructions: Learn lists, slicing, tuples, dictionaries, sets and nested collections, then functions with parameters, return values and local scope. Write functions that take a list of dictionaries (records) and return filtered, sorted or aggregated results. Include at least one function that uses a set to find unique values and one that returns a nested structure. Test each function with a small hand-written list of records.
activities.completionCriterion: A module of at least three functions operating on a list of dictionaries that correctly filter, aggregate and return results, verified on hand-written test data.

activities.title: Read, validate and write data files
activities.purpose: Connect the program to real data by reading files, parsing formats, validating records and handling errors.
activities.instructions: Learn file reading and writing with explicit encodings, CSV parsing, JSON parsing, exceptions and data validation. Create a small CSV file with a few records, some deliberately malformed. Write a script that opens the file with an explicit encoding, parses it with the csv module, validates each record (e.g. required fields present, numeric fields parse), skips or reports invalid rows using try/except, and writes the valid records to a new file. Run it and confirm the output file contains only valid records.
activities.completionCriterion: A script that reads a CSV with at least one malformed row, reports or skips the malformed row without crashing, and writes the valid records to an output file.

activities.title: Group, sort and print a summary report
activities.purpose: Turn validated records into the grouped, sorted summary report that is the first checkpoint outcome.
activities.instructions: Learn grouping and aggregation with dictionaries, sorting records with sorted and key functions, and date parsing with the datetime module. Extend the previous script so it groups valid records by a field, computes counts or sums per group, sorts the groups, and prints a formatted summary report. Wrap the transformation in a reusable function. Run it on the CSV from the previous activity and check the totals by hand.
activities.completionCriterion: A script that reads the CSV, groups and aggregates valid records, sorts the groups and prints a formatted summary report whose totals match a hand calculation.

activities.title: Modules, tests, logging and CLI for the program
activities.purpose: Make the working program reliable and maintainable with modules, tests, logging, a CLI and clear decomposition.
activities.instructions: Learn modules and imports, virtual environments and package installation, simple tests with assert or unittest, boundary cases, logging, command-line arguments with sys.argv or argparse, program decomposition, readable naming, basic debugging and input contracts. Refactor the data-processing script into at least two modules, add tests for the transformation functions including empty and single-record boundary cases, add logging for skipped invalid rows, and accept the input file path as a command-line argument. Run the tests and the program from the command line.
activities.completionCriterion: The program is split into modules, has passing tests covering at least one boundary case, logs skipped rows, accepts an input path as a command-line argument and runs end to end from the command line.

activities.title: Small data-processing project end to end
activities.purpose: Demonstrate the accepted outcome by delivering a complete small data-processing program on a new data file.
activities.instructions: Choose a small real or realistic data file (CSV or JSON) that you have not used before. Build a program that reads it, validates records, handles errors, groups and aggregates, sorts the results and prints or writes a summary report. Use the modules, tests, logging and CLI structure from the previous activity. Run it end to end and verify the report against a hand-checked subset of the data.
activities.completionCriterion: A working program on a new data file that reads, validates, transforms and reports correctly, with tests passing and the report verified against a hand-checked subset.

grounds.excerpt: Keep the full strategic scope, but detail only the useful next checkpoint and forecast later work separately.

Refactor the data-processing script into at least two modules, add tests for the transformation functions including empty and single-record boundary cases, add logging for skipped invalid rows, and accept the input file path as a command-line argument.

finding.evidence: The accepted goal explicitly asks to detail only the useful next checkpoint and forecast later work separately. The strategy's own stopping condition is 'Stop the detailed plan at the first checkpoint: a working program that reads a CSV, validates and groups records and prints a sorted summary report.' Yet engineering_practices is a COMMITTED activity that requires modules, tests, logging, CLI and decomposition (scope_28-36, 38) and is scheduled on 2026-10-07, and project_delivery is a further COMMITTED full project on a new data file scheduled 2026-10-08. These are later-phase work that the goal said to forecast separately, not commit now.
finding.consequence: The learner is committed to complete engineering-practice and second-project work beyond the accepted next checkpoint, changing what must be finished and contradicting the explicit 'detail only the useful next checkpoint' instruction.
finding.requestedResolution: Remove engineering_practices and project_delivery from the committed detail; keep phase_engineering and phase_project as forecast-only phases. Detail and commit only the checkpoint activities (core_basics, collections_functions, files_csv_validation, transform_report) unless the learner explicitly requests expansion.

grounds.excerpt: A single script that uses variables, at least one conditional, one while or for loop and formatted output, runs without errors and produces the expected result on two different inputs.

finding.evidence: The completion criterion requires the script to 'run without errors and produce the expected result on two different inputs' but does not state what the expected result is or how it is verified, so a learner could satisfy it by asserting their own output is expected. The criterion is otherwise concrete about constructs used.
finding.consequence: Completion may be recorded without a checkable correctness standard for the core-language checkpoint, weakening the evidence that later activities depend on.
finding.requestedResolution: State the expected output for the two inputs (or a hand-checkable rule) so the criterion can be verified independently, or accept the criterion as sufficient for a foundational checkpoint.

grounds.excerpt: Actual pace and retention are unknown; the effort estimates may need revision after the first checkpoint.

finding.evidence: The plan honestly records that pace and retention are unknown and that estimates may need revision, and the allocation flags ESTIMATE_RISK because timeboxes (30 min) are far below likely effort (150-300 min).
finding.consequence: The learner may reach timebox boundaries without completing activities; the plan already treats this as a checkpoint for revision rather than a failure.
finding.requestedResolution: Retain as an honest assumption; revisit effort estimates after the first checkpoint produces evidence.

## Cambridge International A Level Physics 9702 revision checklist FAQ
Quick answers about this free revision checklist, how to use it for exam prep, and how it relates to the official syllabus.
What does the 2026 Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 syllabus cover? This revision checklist mirrors the official Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 syllabus for the 2026 examination series. Every topic and sub-topic on the page is taken from the published syllabus document, so working through the list in order gives you full coverage of what your exam can assess. It is aligned to the A Level tier expectations. For the authoritative version, always cross-check with the latest syllabus PDF on your exam board's website before your final revision push.
How many topics are on the Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 exam? The number of top-level topic groups varies by subject, but you can see the exact count on this page — each major heading in the checklist corresponds to one syllabus topic group, and each row below it is a syllabus-level sub-topic. Use the confidence column (1–5) to flag which sub-topics need more work, and re-score yourself weekly to track real progress instead of guessing.
How long should I spend revising for Cambridge A Level Physics 9702? 12–16 weeks of focused revision, working through one topic group per week with weekly past-paper practice, is a realistic target for most A Level students. Use this checklist to plan your weeks: filter by topics you have rated 1–3 and spend your first revision block there. Subjects with heavy practical or extended-writing components (e.g. sciences, English) need more past-paper time in the final block than the topic-by-topic phase.
What's the best order to revise Physics topics? Revise in roughly the order the syllabus lists the topics — exam boards build later topics on earlier ones, so taking them in syllabus order avoids gaps. Once you have rated every topic, switch to weakest-first: filter the checklist by confidence ≤ 2 and prioritise those topics in your next study block. This is more effective than re-revising topics you already score 4–5 on.
Where can I find Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 past papers and mark schemes? You can find past papers and mark schemes via Tutopiya's Past Paper Finder and on your exam board's official site. Once you have rated each sub-topic on this checklist, attempt past-paper questions on your weakest topics first — practising under timed conditions is the single best predictor of exam performance, more so than re-reading notes.
How do I download this revision checklist as a PDF or CSV? Use the Download CSV or Print PDF button at the bottom of the checklist. CSV opens in Excel, Numbers or Google Sheets so you can sort by confidence and re-arrange revision order. The PDF is print-ready for offline use. A free Tutopiya account is required for download — this also unlocks the matching topic resources, notes and worked examples on the Learning Portal .
Is this Physics revision checklist free to use? Yes, the checklist itself is free — you can view, score and re-score every topic on this page without an account. The CSV / PDF downloads and access to matching Tutopiya Learning Portal resources require a free account. There is no payment required at any point; teachers and parents can also use this checklist freely with their students.
Does this checklist match the latest Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 specification? Yes. The topics and sub-topics on this page are drawn from the current 2026 Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 specification published by Cambridge. Exam boards occasionally tweak weighting or assessment structure mid-cycle, so do a quick sanity-check against the official syllabus PDF when you start your revision and again 4 weeks before the exam.

## Cambridge International A Level Physics 9702 revision checklist FAQ
Quick answers about this free revision checklist, how to use it for exam prep, and how it relates to the official syllabus.
What does the 2026 Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 syllabus cover? This revision checklist mirrors the official Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 syllabus for the 2026 examination series. Every topic and sub-topic on the page is taken from the published syllabus document, so working through the list in order gives you full coverage of what your exam can assess. It is aligned to the A Level tier expectations. For the authoritative version, always cross-check with the latest syllabus PDF on your exam board's website before your final revision push.
How many topics are on the Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 exam? The number of top-level topic groups varies by subject, but you can see the exact count on this page — each major heading in the checklist corresponds to one syllabus topic group, and each row below it is a syllabus-level sub-topic. Use the confidence column (1–5) to flag which sub-topics need more work, and re-score yourself weekly to track real progress instead of guessing.
How long should I spend revising for Cambridge A Level Physics 9702? 12–16 weeks of focused revision, working through one topic group per week with weekly past-paper practice, is a realistic target for most A Level students. Use this checklist to plan your weeks: filter by topics you have rated 1–3 and spend your first revision block there. Subjects with heavy practical or extended-writing components (e.g. sciences, English) need more past-paper time in the final block than the topic-by-topic phase.
What's the best order to revise Physics topics? Revise in roughly the order the syllabus lists the topics — exam boards build later topics on earlier ones, so taking them in syllabus order avoids gaps. Once you have rated every topic, switch to weakest-first: filter the checklist by confidence ≤ 2 and prioritise those topics in your next study block. This is more effective than re-revising topics you already score 4–5 on.
Where can I find Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 past papers and mark schemes? You can find past papers and mark schemes via Tutopiya's Past Paper Finder and on your exam board's official site. Once you have rated each sub-topic on this checklist, attempt past-paper questions on your weakest topics first — practising under timed conditions is the single best predictor of exam performance, more so than re-reading notes.
How do I download this revision checklist as a PDF or CSV? Use the Download CSV or Print PDF button at the bottom of the checklist. CSV opens in Excel, Numbers or Google Sheets so you can sort by confidence and re-arrange revision order. The PDF is print-ready for offline use. A free Tutopiya account is required for download — this also unlocks the matching topic resources, notes and worked examples on the Learning Portal .
Is this Physics revision checklist free to use? Yes, the checklist itself is free — you can view, score and re-score every topic on this page without an account. The CSV / PDF downloads and access to matching Tutopiya Learning Portal resources require a free account. There is no payment required at any point; teachers and parents can also use this checklist freely with their students.
Does this checklist match the latest Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 specification? Yes. The topics and sub-topics on this page are drawn from the current 2026 Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 specification published by Cambridge. Exam boards occasionally tweak weighting or assessment structure mid-cycle, so do a quick sanity-check against the official syllabus PDF when you start your revision and again 4 weeks before the exam.

## Cambridge International A Level Physics 9702 revision checklist FAQ
Quick answers about this free revision checklist, how to use it for exam prep, and how it relates to the official syllabus.
What does the 2026 Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 syllabus cover? This revision checklist mirrors the official Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 syllabus for the 2026 examination series. Every topic and sub-topic on the page is taken from the published syllabus document, so working through the list in order gives you full coverage of what your exam can assess. It is aligned to the A Level tier expectations. For the authoritative version, always cross-check with the latest syllabus PDF on your exam board's website before your final revision push.
How many topics are on the Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 exam? The number of top-level topic groups varies by subject, but you can see the exact count on this page — each major heading in the checklist corresponds to one syllabus topic group, and each row below it is a syllabus-level sub-topic. Use the confidence column (1–5) to flag which sub-topics need more work, and re-score yourself weekly to track real progress instead of guessing.
How long should I spend revising for Cambridge A Level Physics 9702? 12–16 weeks of focused revision, working through one topic group per week with weekly past-paper practice, is a realistic target for most A Level students. Use this checklist to plan your weeks: filter by topics you have rated 1–3 and spend your first revision block there. Subjects with heavy practical or extended-writing components (e.g. sciences, English) need more past-paper time in the final block than the topic-by-topic phase.
What's the best order to revise Physics topics? Revise in roughly the order the syllabus lists the topics — exam boards build later topics on earlier ones, so taking them in syllabus order avoids gaps. Once you have rated every topic, switch to weakest-first: filter the checklist by confidence ≤ 2 and prioritise those topics in your next study block. This is more effective than re-revising topics you already score 4–5 on.
Where can I find Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 past papers and mark schemes? You can find past papers and mark schemes via Tutopiya's Past Paper Finder and on your exam board's official site. Once you have rated each sub-topic on this checklist, attempt past-paper questions on your weakest topics first — practising under timed conditions is the single best predictor of exam performance, more so than re-reading notes.
How do I download this revision checklist as a PDF or CSV? Use the Download CSV or Print PDF button at the bottom of the checklist. CSV opens in Excel, Numbers or Google Sheets so you can sort by confidence and re-arrange revision order. The PDF is print-ready for offline use. A free Tutopiya account is required for download — this also unlocks the matching topic resources, notes and worked examples on the Learning Portal .
Is this Physics revision checklist free to use? Yes, the checklist itself is free — you can view, score and re-score every topic on this page without an account. The CSV / PDF downloads and access to matching Tutopiya Learning Portal resources require a free account. There is no payment required at any point; teachers and parents can also use this checklist freely with their students.
Does this checklist match the latest Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 specification? Yes. The topics and sub-topics on this page are drawn from the current 2026 Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 specification published by Cambridge. Exam boards occasionally tweak weighting or assessment structure mid-cycle, so do a quick sanity-check against the official syllabus PDF when you start your revision and again 4 weeks before the exam.
